summary: The EmailPopupDocument module manages the creation, retrieval, and deletion of email attachments or documents, handling them in-memory using a pipe-separated string representation for temporary storage. It provides mechanisms to parse, list, and remove documents including associated filesystem operations.
purpose: To facilitate the lifecycle of documents used in email popups, specifically for searching, displaying, and deleting documents (and folders) as needed during the email composition or sending workflow.

fields.name: ID
fields.description: Unique in-session identifier for each document entry. Initialized to -1 in the constructor.

fields.name: FileName
fields.description: The display or attachment file name.

fields.name: FilePath
fields.description: The path to the file for further operations, such as deletion.

fields.name: Checked
fields.description: Boolean indicating if the item is checked (usage not fully detailed in content).

actors: User (triggering document selection/deletion in UI or workflow)

workflows.name: Search for Email Popup Documents
steps: Receive raw data string (DataInfo), typically pipe-separated values.
Split DataInfo using '|' delimiter into individual entries.
For each entry, split using '>' to separate FileName and FilePath.
For valid entries (length == 2), instantiate EmailPopupDocument objects, set properties (ID, FileName, FilePath), append to result list.
Return the list of EmailPopupDocument instances for display or further handling.

workflows.name: Delete Email Popup Document
steps: Receive pipe-separated data string (DataInfo) and target document ID (index).
When the current index matches the supplied ID:
- Split entry using '>' to get FilePath.
- Attempt to delete the file at FilePath (ignore errors).
- Attempt to delete the directory (ignore errors).
All other entries are retained into a return string.
Return the updated DataInfo string, now missing the deleted document.

business_rules: Only entries with two segments after splitting by '>' are considered valid email documents.
IDs are assigned incrementally during parsing and are positional (array index based).
validations: Check if provided DataInfo is not null or empty before performing operations.
For delete operation, ensure DataInfo is not null or empty and ID is valid (indexable).
calculations: ID is incrementally assigned in the order of parsing valid documents.
conditions: Deletion only proceeds if the index matches the provided ID and the split entry is valid.
system_behavior: On delete, errors in deleting files or directories are caught and ignored (fail silently).
All document lifecycle logic is handled in-memory using string manipulation and not persisted beyond the session unless further context is provided.
dependencies: System.IO for file and directory operations.
Data is managed via in-memory string parsing rather than persisted data storage.
exceptions: Try/catch blocks around file and directory deletion: failures are ignored and do not halt the method.
